newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-US T-bond futures seen rising in near term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-US T-bond futures seen rising in near term.

text.p: U.S. T-bond futures are expected to rally in the near term, with bullish technical factors for the September contract improving in its first day as lead month, technical analysts said.
September T-bonds, which became lead contract month at the start of Thursday's evening session, began Friday's pit trade on a firm footing and recently extended gains to 109-16/32.

"The technical situtation has really improved after we once again rejected the seven percent level (on cash long bond)," one T-bond futures analyst said. The 7.00 percent level currently corresponds to 108-05/32 in September.
The 108-05/32 level is also the 50-day moving average.
Traders are pegging intraday support at 109-04/32 to 109-07/32, an area broached soon after revisions to U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product were released.
"It had a chance to break earlier, but didn't," Bernard Savaiko, futures research director at PaineWebber Inc, said about the positive tone of September bonds.
He said the 110-00 level, which is a May-December trendline, is a valid objective, and that a close above 110-09/32, the three-month high, would pave the way for a rise to 110-29/32.
The 110-09/32 level is equivalent to a yield level of 6.82 percent, analysts said.
Savaiko said the relative strength index was neutral but had turned slightly higher with the early-morning rally that initially took September bonds to 109-14/32.
"I'm surprised we got to 109-17/32," one floor trader said about September's subsequent rally at midsession.
"I'm thinking that we can carry this to 109-23/32," he said.
The 109-23/32 level is a 200-day moving average and correponds to a yield of 6.86 percent.
However, one bond market analyst remained a little skeptical of September's strength.

"When you change contract months there is an idea that the different months have different characteristics, but I'm skeptical of September's ability to run higher," he said, noting June T-bonds' inability to close above some key resistance levels in the last week.
He said the short-term bearish trend would resume if September failed to hold above 109-00 on Friday. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
